references.text: The preceding verse introduces the loops of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn on the edges of the linen curtains, which verse 5 continues to describe in detail.
The next verse describes the fifty gold clasps that were to be used to fasten the loops together so that the tabernacle would become one whole.
A parallel construction with fifty loops for the goat-hair tent curtains, following the same pattern as the loops on the linen curtains.
The fulfillment of the instruction in 26:5, where the craftsmen actually make the fifty loops on each curtain that correspond to one another.
A parallel execution of fifty loops on the goat-hair tent curtains, mirroring the pattern from the linen curtains.
The loops from the source verse are necessary to fasten the tent together into a single unit via the clasps.
Both verses demonstrate the theological principle that separate parts must be joined together into one whole.
